k.justification: k=8 from the checkpoint sd of 0.05-0.09 and a sqrt(k) noise reduction: 8 checkpoints take 0.05-0.09 to 0.018-0.032, which is the scale of the differences the nb3 table tries to resolve. k=1 IS the existing single-point read-off and is the comparison basis, not a new estimator. k=2 and k=4 are declared here so the sqrt(k) curve has interior points; they are reported whatever they show.

metric.primary: TPR@FPR=1e-3, interpolated, drop_intermediate=False, always a rate
metric.undefined_values: n/a with no CI and no fold-mean, as everywhere else

no_significance_claims_beyond_the_declar: the unit is the fold, n=4 (n=5 for Baseline A). Paired t on differences, df=n-1, exactly as 7.22 and 7.28. Never a bootstrap at n=4.

scatter_test.a_large_shortfall_means: the checkpoint noise is autocorrelated rather than independent, which is itself a reportable line
scatter_test.estimator: for each arm and fold, slide the k-window over EVERY valid position on that arm's own checkpoint grid, compute the metric at each position, and take the sd across positions. Compare against the same fold's k=1 sd computed on the same set of positions, so the two sds are over the same steps.
scatter_test.question: does the achieved scatter reduction match the sqrt(k) expectation?

BNM x nb3.note: 1000 is no_matched_arm_budget; 4000 is the mandatory one

Baseline A (frozen).note: round-1 R1 last-checkpoint. Only step_8000 scores were retained, so the per-checkpoint score vectors are RECOMPUTED on CPU from the frozen 640-d feature cache and the retained per-step head weights. No GPU, no training.

scope.note: every arm and both baselines, at every mandatory readout. Read-off steps are copied from each arm's own pre-registration/budget record; none is chosen here.

primary.name: mean_logit
primary.rule: arithmetic mean, per image, of the RAW saved logits over the window's checkpoints; the metric is then computed once on the averaged score vector

secondary.name: mean_rank
secondary.rule: per checkpoint, replace each image's logit by its rank over that checkpoint's full eval pool divided by (N-1) so it lies in [0,1]; average those across the window. Scale-free.
secondary.why_declared: mean_logit is the literal reading of 'average scores', but it is not invariant to a checkpoint whose logit scale has drifted: one wide-scale checkpoint can dominate the mean and the window would then be a single-point read-off wearing a disguise. mean_rank cannot do that. Both are declared NOW and BOTH are reported for every arm; neither is promoted after the fact.

score_combination.weights_are_never_averaged: scores only. Averaging weights across checkpoints of an unfrozen encoder is a different and unlicensed intervention.

status: DECLARED SECONDARY ANALYSIS -- replaces no hashed headline
the_verdict_it_owes: 7.16 records nine orderings as dissolved. This analysis must state, for each ordering that a read-off choice could plausibly have caused, whether it SURVIVES window averaging or NOT. Orderings survived => the limit is in the data and 7.16 is stronger than nine anecdotes. Orderings did not survive => the read-off choice was the fault, the fix is located, and 7.16's affected entries get updated rather than left standing alongside a contradicting claim.

what_this_is_not.hashed_headlines_stand: every pre-registered single-point number in 7.12, 7.15, 7.18, 7.22 and 7.28 remains the arm's reported result

why: Single-point read-off is the noisiest estimator available. 7.16's eighth entry measures a within-run checkpoint sd of 0.0402-0.0914 on fold 0 against between-method differences of 0.018, and fold 0's BNM curve moves 0.5102 -> 0.2857 across one 250-step gap. Averaging k consecutive checkpoints' SCORES reduces that scatter by sqrt(k) IF the checkpoint noise is independent. Whether it actually does is the measurement.

window_placement.placed_by: the pre-registered read-off point -- so the rule reads no metric
window_placement.rule: the k consecutive AVAILABLE checkpoints ending AT the pre-registered read-off step, inclusive of that step
window_placement.step_0_excluded: step 0 is the initialisation, not a trained checkpoint; it never enters a window
window_placement.truncation: where fewer than k trained checkpoints exist at or before the read-off, the window is truncated to all that do exist and the ACHIEVED k is reported next to the value
